scope: Native Kimi device issuer/login/live CLI composition across standalone, interactive, startup/listing/reload/print/JSON/RPC

requirements.requirement: Guarded native issuer login and canonical CLI admission without selection
requirements.implementation: security/kimi-login.ts reserves the existing encrypted credential slot before Core native Device work, verifies terminal-safe instructions, publishes the typed native grant and checks caller/host again after return. Standalone auth login and interactive /login explicitly accept --issuer kimi-coding; no issuer is inferred from the storage label. Existing public-client host aliases choose the issuer; instructions preserve the code but strip URL query values. Native Kimi is device-only. Canonical label becomes available, not selected; foreign labels remain passive. No browser/listener/opener or generic endpoint retargeting is added.
requirements.proof: Shared existing Radius command fixture adds canonical/foreign Kimi cases, held absent-slot logout and already-committed/retired-helper return, while all seven Radius cases remain. Existing27 actual emitted auth/TLS paths retain no-inferred-issuer/help/cancel/deadline/privacy/generic controls; the Kimi stored-refresh journey now explicitly asserts native issuer/realm, ordinary-consumer refusal, stable grant and live SDK dispatch instead of a generic token snapshot.

requirements.implementation: CliKimiOAuth retains private administrative metadata plus a live Core credential resolver, never a token in runtime.values. Online bootstrap reads the loaded native snapshot without refresh; offline bootstrap requires locally fresh expiry. Only a selected SDK operation may refresh. Explicit realm mismatch refuses before I/O, and selected key/command sources retain priority. Configured native constructor, startup/listing/reload/RPC and interactive mounting carry the resolver; factories remain authoritative without receiving OAuth tokens. Ephemeral key override recreates the old key adapter and preserves the configured endpoint. Legacy unmarked OAuth and API-key behavior remain separate.
requirements.proof: Seven new runtime cases cover live refresh/inference/logout, key/command-offline/expired-offline/realm refusal, runtime/per-operation lifetime clipping and passive expired bootstrap before invocation key. One configured-provider case adds native/source/factory/ephemeral-key boundaries. A focused old-image passive-bootstrap RED catches premature refresh; administrative snapshot bootstrap corrects it without an extra option or provider-resolution framework.

requirements.requirement: Useful emitted native Kimi private continuation across actual process refresh and offline resolution
requirements.implementation: The native facade and existing private session/tool-loop/policy mechanisms are consumed by real CLI modes. Persisted issuer/local grant survives a new process without host environment hints; only access credentials rotate. Static Kimi models are not account entitlement, and no new account catalogue/cache is introduced.
requirements.proof: Three new loopback verified-TLS print/JSON/RPC journeys perform native device login, signed thinking/text inference, encrypted expiry, a new-process native refresh/replay, a third-process offline-source replay and logout refusal. Exact old vendor signatures reach all resumed A histories with no harness wrapper on wire. Each assistant records physical kimi-coding/k3/anthropic-messages and10 tokens/$0.000054; one refresh preserves the local grant. Six issuer/inference requests per mode,18 total, no account-discovery requests.0600 credentials and journals/public outputs omit synthetic credentials; public output omits private signatures.

Expired stored Kimi invokes refresh before ephemeral --api-key selection. Native online bootstrap now uses administrative metadata, not a request resolver.

The native-Kimi positive TLS response now supplies a public-code verification_uri_complete instead of embedding the private device code, matching the Core native instruction contract. The separate generic private-query fixture and existing privacy assertions remain unchanged. Existing stored-Kimi SDK checks are strengthened for the requested new native credential/issuer contract, not relaxed to accept a legacy flattened token.
